text_summary: OISD Standard 137 governs hot work operations in hydrocarbon processing facilities. All hot work within 15 metres of a potential hydrocarbon source requires a valid hot work permit with gas testing at the work site and all adjacent drain points. Continuous gas monitoring must be maintained throughout the work duration, with monitoring frequency increased to every 15 minutes when ambient temperature exceeds 40°C. The fire watch must remain on station for 30 minutes after work completion and possess a 9 kg DCP extinguisher within arm's reach.

DGMS Circular 04/2023 mandates a structured shift handover process at all major hazard installations. The outgoing shift supervisor must complete a written handover log covering all active permits, abnormal conditions, overridden safety interlocks, and any equipment operating outside normal parameters. A face-to-face verbal briefing of at least 10 minutes is required. No permit-to-work may be newly issued during the 30-minute handover window. The incoming supervisor must physically verify the status of any equipment tagged for abnormal operation before assuming charge.

OISD Guideline 216 defines confined space entry procedures for petroleum and petrochemical installations. Entry requires atmospheric testing for O2 (19.5–23.5%), LEL (<1%), and toxic gases (H2S <10 ppm, CO <35 ppm) at multiple levels within the space. A standby person must be stationed at the entry point at all times with rescue equipment including a full-body harness, lifeline, and self-contained breathing apparatus. Continuous forced ventilation must be maintained, and re-testing is required if ventilation is interrupted for any period.

DGMS Circular 11/2022 establishes gas monitoring requirements for industrial plants handling toxic and flammable gases. Fixed gas detectors must be calibrated at intervals not exceeding 90 days using certified reference gases traceable to national standards. Portable monitors used for permit-to-work verification must be bump-tested at the start of each shift. Any detector showing drift greater than 10% of span must be removed from service immediately and recalibrated. Facilities must maintain a minimum of two spare calibrated detectors per zone as backup.

OISD Standard 144 prescribes the permit-to-work system for petroleum refineries and petrochemical plants. Permits are classified as cold work, hot work, confined space entry, excavation, electrical isolation, and radiography. Each permit must specify the exact work scope, equipment boundaries, isolation points, and required PPE. No more than one active permit per equipment item is allowed unless a cross-referencing multi-permit assessment is completed by the plant safety officer. Permits are valid for a maximum of 12 hours and must be re-validated for each subsequent shift.

The Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO) Static and Mobile Pressure Vessels Rules 2016 require periodic inspection of all pressure vessels at intervals not exceeding 36 months or at each turnaround, whichever is sooner. Inspection includes external visual examination, internal examination where accessible, ultrasonic thickness measurement at predetermined grid points, and non-destructive testing of all nozzle welds. Vessels showing corrosion rates exceeding the design corrosion allowance divided by remaining design life must be reported to the Chief Controller of Explosives within 30 days.
